title: Maximum Students Taking Exam
summary: Given a m * n matrix seats indicating seat conditions with '#' for broken seats and '.' for usable seats, determine the maximum number of students that can sit without any student cheating by seeing another's answers.
statement: Given a m * n matrix seats indicating seat conditions with '#' for broken seats and '.' for usable seats, determine the maximum number of students that can sit without any student cheating by seeing another's answers. Ensure all students sit in unbroken seats and cannot see the answers of those directly in front or behind them.
constraints: A dot is usable and a hash is broken.
Students cannot occupy horizontally adjacent seats or diagonally adjacent seats in consecutive rows; vertical adjacency is allowed.
Return the greatest number of students that can be seated.
hints: Represent occupied seats in each row as a bitmask.
Enumerate submasks of usable seats that contain no adjacent bits.
Combine a row mask with prior masks only when neither diagonal shift intersects.
Every legal layout has one legal mask per row, and the DP maximizes over every compatible sequence.
editorial: For each row, enumerate masks contained in its usable-seat mask and reject horizontal adjacency. Dynamic programming combines each legal mask with compatible previous-row masks by testing both diagonal shifts. The oracle independently enumerates every subset of usable positions on seeded boards and checks forbidden coordinate pairs directly.

tests.explanation: Four usable seats can be chosen without a forbidden horizontal or diagonal pair.
The two usable seats are diagonally adjacent, so only one student can sit.
